classificationDefinitions.ENFORCED: an executable artefact proves it (test, verifier script, migration, policy or machine-checked contract match) and, where a boundary is declared, a real call site invokes it
classificationDefinitions.DECLARED: a module, document or contract mentions it, but nothing executable proves it
classificationDefinitions.IMPLEMENTED_UNWIRED: implementation and tests exist, but the declared boundary patterns match nothing — the capability protects nothing yet

ownership.note: Phase 09 owns trust state, trust evidence and assurance; it never owns enforcement. Phase 08 answers 'may this action happen?' and Phase 09 answers 'how much should CoreGrid trust the entities, evidence and relationships involved?' (BS). Identity is Phase 02's, tenancy Phase 03's, the agent runtime Phase 07's, data classification Phase 14's, the adversarial-defense engine Phase 42's.

areas.area: Trust subjects and the subject vocabulary
areas.requirement: Trust subjects can be registered across the documented kinds (person, organization, institution, tenant, device, agent, service, application, workload, software, artifact, data source) and begin as UNKNOWN.

areas.area: Trust state vocabulary and usability
areas.requirement: The ten states of F.3 exist, and the fabric distinguishes usable from non-usable states without ever treating UNKNOWN as trust.

areas.area: Trust state machine (legal transitions only)
areas.requirement: Trust moves only along declared transitions, and the machine refuses illegal moves as a value rather than throwing.

areas.area: UNKNOWN cannot silently become TRUSTED (BR.10, BO.16)
areas.requirement: A subject cannot move from UNKNOWN to a trusted state directly, or by skipping the VERIFIED step; evidence is required to withdraw trust.

areas.area: REVOKED is terminal (BR.4)
areas.requirement: No transition leaves REVOKED; restoration requires a new, evidenced establishment.

areas.area: Trust relationships and the 13 relationship types (I, AO)
areas.requirement: Trust relationships are recorded with type, source, target, tenant scope and evidence, and an evidence-free relationship is refused.

areas.area: Trust expiry (AB, BO.7)
areas.requirement: Trust relationships expire, and revocation takes effect immediately; expired trust never silently remains valid.

areas.area: Multi-tenant trust (AN, BR.15)
areas.requirement: Trust relationships and assertions carry tenant scope where applicable, and cross-tenant trust is explicit — never inferred.

areas.area: Trust scoring (K)
areas.requirement: Trust scores are evidence-weighted confidence computed from declared factors, and a score without factors or with invalid confidence is refused.

areas.area: Score properties: explainable, versioned, contextual, time-sensitive, evidence-backed (K.3, BR.9)
areas.requirement: A score carries its factor breakdown, evidence references, version, evaluation time and context, and it never replaces the evidence it summarises.

areas.area: Trust assertions (F.1, L.2)
areas.requirement: An assertion carries id, issuer, subject, type, trust level, evidence, issue and expiry, scope, tenant, integrity reference and provenance — and it is refused without issuer, subject, evidence or integrity protection.

areas.area: Assertion verification (L, O.2, AB, BR.7, BO.3)
areas.requirement: Verification fails on unchecked integrity, revocation, expiry, an unaccepted issuer or a scope mismatch, and passes only when all of them hold.

areas.area: Trust evidence quality (M.2)
areas.requirement: Evidence carries source, capture time, freshness window, reliability, integrity reference, provenance and confidence, and stale evidence is detected rather than reused.

areas.area: Trust provenance — 'why does CoreGrid trust this?' (N.1, N.2, N.3, BO.5)
areas.requirement: A provenance chain starts from the trust decision and must reference evidence; every important assertion is traceable to its source.

areas.area: Trust revocation — reasons, kinds, attribution (AA, BO.8)
areas.requirement: Revocation can be recorded for the eight documented reasons as temporary suspension, permanent revocation, quarantine or conditional restoration, requires an attributable actor, and requires a condition for conditional restoration.

areas.area: Key trust registry (P) and certificate trust (Q, BO.9)
areas.requirement: Key metadata is registered without private material and expires; certificates are registered, refuse an already-expired certificate, and fail validation on expiry, revocation or an unverified chain.

areas.area: Device trust (S, BO.10)
areas.requirement: Device trust is computed from security-relevant facts (enrolment, posture, OS integrity, encryption, attestation, anomalies), and missing enrolment or failed attestation never produces a trusted state.

areas.area: Workload trust (T, BO.11)
areas.requirement: Workload trust evaluates deployment origin, artifact integrity, image provenance and configuration integrity, and an unverified workload is never trusted.

areas.area: Agent trust (U, BO.12) — degradation never grants
areas.requirement: Agent trust considers identity, policy compliance, tool behaviour, execution history and prompt integrity; suspicious tool behaviour quarantines, and degradation never adds permissions.

areas.area: Model trust (V)
areas.requirement: Model trust records provenance, version, integrity, evaluation result, approved-use scope and rollback version, and a model missing any of provenance, integrity or evaluation is UNVERIFIED.

areas.area: Software provenance, artifact integrity and supply-chain trust (W, X, Y, BO.13)
areas.requirement: Software provenance records repository, commit, build, dependencies, signer and environment; artifact integrity fails on a hash mismatch or missing signature; unverifiable provenance reduces trust to UNVERIFIED or DEGRADED.

areas.area: Trust federation and external trust (AC, AD, BO.14)
areas.requirement: Every federation defines parties, scope, accepted assertions, verification methods, expiry, revocation and audit requirement; external trust is never unrestricted internal trust.

areas.area: Trust delegation (AG)
areas.requirement: A delegation names delegator, delegate, authority, scope, expiry and restrictions, refuses self-delegation, and is traceable.

areas.area: Trust anchor management (AI, BR.12)
areas.requirement: Anchors (root certificates, root keys, approved issuers, registries, identity providers, signing authorities) require an identified managing administrator and can be revoked.

areas.area: Trust policy registry — versioned requirements (AE)
areas.requirement: Trust policies are versioned and define accepted issuers, acceptable evidence, trust lifetimes, minimum assurance and attestation requirements; evaluation refuses an unaccepted issuer, unaccepted evidence, missing attestation and assurance below the minimum.

areas.area: Zero-trust evaluation (AK) — verdicts, never enforcement (BS)
areas.requirement: The zero-trust principles produce a trust verdict (deny, challenge, trusted) from identity, session, device trust and the Phase 08 risk action, and the verdict is advice rather than enforcement.

areas.area: Human escalation for high-impact trust changes (BM)
areas.requirement: Adding a root anchor, approving a federation, restoring a compromised subject, changing organization-wide policy, accepting a new certificate authority or overriding a critical revocation require human approval.

areas.area: Trust graph traversal and revocation propagation (I, BR.11)
areas.requirement: Relationships between trusted entities are represented as a graph, and revocation propagates to dependents.

areas.area: Cryptographic trust service and agility (O, AX)
areas.requirement: Machine-verifiable trust: signature creation and verification, key ownership, certificate chains, rotation, revocation, artifact signing and data-integrity verification, with configurable algorithms.

areas.area: Attestation lifecycle (R)
areas.requirement: Claims about system state (device, workload, software, runtime environment, secure boot, deployment identity) are requested, evidenced, verified and turned into assertions that update trust.

areas.area: Trust data model and database requirements (AO, AP)
areas.requirement: The 22 trust entities are held with immutable identifiers, tenant boundaries, temporal validity, issuer/subject/evidence/provenance/revocation references — and private cryptographic material never enters ordinary storage.

areas.area: Trust information consumed by Phase 08 (AL, BS, BO.15)
areas.requirement: The Security Engine consumes trust state, score, assertion verification, provenance, attestation and revocation so that enforcement decisions carry assurance context.

areas.area: Trust observability (BA)
areas.requirement: Trust evaluation latency, state changes, assertion failures, revocations, attestation and provenance failures, certificate expiry and score instability are monitored.

areas.area: Service trust records and security posture records (G.16, Z)
areas.requirement: Service trust state and trust-relevant security posture (patch status, certificate status, credential age, configuration status, integrity status, attestation status, control status) are represented as records.

areas.area: Trust agents (AU, AV) and MCP interfaces (AT)
areas.requirement: Trust analysis, provenance, investigation, supply-chain, attestation, federation and governance agents operate under least privilege, and trust MCP capabilities are exposed behind Phase 08 enforcement.

areas.area: Security and adversarial testing (BE.3, BF, BO.20)
areas.requirement: Forged assertions, replay, trust escalation, malicious federation, revoked-credential reuse, invalid certificates, provenance tampering, chain manipulation, compromised issuers and stale evidence are tested as attacks.

areas.area: External trust integration with real providers (AD, AS)
areas.requirement: Federation with schools, universities, government, payment providers, identity providers, cloud providers and marketplaces, with signed webhooks, replay protection, delivery tracking and secret rotation.

areas.area: Reliability, reliability failure modes, disaster recovery and operating procedures (BB, BC, BD, BL)
areas.requirement: Trust infrastructure is highly available with replication, backup and recovery; UNKNOWN is never silently converted to TRUSTED; and anchor rotation, compromised-issuer response, federation suspension and policy rollback are documented and rehearsed.

areas.area: Trust migration (BY)
areas.requirement: Trust records survive schema, policy, anchor, algorithm, tenant, federation and recovery migration without losing provenance, and a revocation always wins over a migrated record.

areas.area: Phase boundary with the Security Engine (D.1, BS)
areas.requirement: Phase 08 owns runtime authorization, enforcement, policy execution, alerts, incident runtime, rate limiting and enforcement middleware; Phase 09 supplies trust and assurance context and duplicates none of it.

areas.area: Phase test suites (BE.1, BE.2)
areas.requirement: Trust calculations, state transitions, assertions, expiration, revocation, provenance and policy evaluation are proven by executable tests, plus identity, engine, agent and tenant integration paths.

areas.area: Deployment and infrastructure (BI, BJ)
areas.requirement: Trust components deploy independently with encryption, isolated trust services, secure key storage, high availability, disaster recovery and controlled administrative access.

areas.area: Runtime consumer boundary (BZ)
areas.requirement: CoreGrid owns the fabric: no kernel module may import a runtime, only a runtime layer may name a runtime, and no platform surface may hard-code a limited role list.

areas.area: Control-plane surface that exercises the fabric (L4)
areas.requirement: The phase has a surface where its behaviour is visible and exercised rather than described.

areas.area: Engineering-section completeness of the phase document
areas.requirement: The document states the mandatory engineering sections, including the command, query, workflow, memory/knowledge and migration models and the runtime consumer boundary.

areas.area: Acceptance criteria and definition of done (BO, BP)
areas.requirement: Phase 09 is accepted only when subjects, relationships, assertions, evidence, provenance, state changes, expiry, revocation and cryptographic trust exist, device/workload/agent/software trust are represented, federation is scoped, Phase 08 can consume trust, UNKNOWN cannot become TRUSTED, changes are auditable, tenant boundaries hold, recovery works and adversarial testing passes.

areas.area: AI-assisted trust evaluation and its limits (BG)
areas.requirement: AI-assisted trust systems are evaluated for false trust, false distrust, evidence and provenance hallucination, reasoning reliability and adversarial manipulation — and AI recommendations cannot silently override deterministic controls.

areas.area: Trust evaluation performance (BH)
areas.requirement: Trust evaluation is optimised through state, evidence and posture caching, efficient graph traversal and indexed provenance, and caching respects expiration and revocation.

areas.area: Compliance evidence (BN)
areas.requirement: The fabric supports evidence for identity assurance, access assurance, provenance, data integrity, software supply-chain integrity, auditability and security controls, without defining legal compliance.

limitations: Classification measures the presence of executable evidence, not the correctness or completeness of that evidence.
A DECLARED area is unfinished work, never a false claim — it is reported as such.
An IMPLEMENTED_UNWIRED area has a tested implementation that no boundary calls; it is reported, never counted as enforcement.
Evidence patterns are declared per phase in architecture/phase-acceptance/phase-<id>-*.json and must be reviewed when a phase is re-audited.
